requirements.title: NAMELIST has slash-delimited named groups with nonempty object lists
requirements.definition: NAMELIST is followed by /group-name/ and a nonempty group-object list. Additional slash-delimited group clauses may follow, each optionally preceded by a comma and each with its own nonempty object list. There is no unnamed group or double-colon alternative. R401 supplies the object lists; the complete grammar-head scan finds no explicit namelist-group-name rule, so R402/R603 supplies that name convention. Actual objects use R872/R903.

pending.single-group: PENDING compile/positive-control in a complete ordinary program with prior INTEGER :: a,b and NAMELIST /group_a/ a,b. There is no data transfer, initializer, assumed-size or enumeration object; all names and types are complete.
pending.multiple-groups-with-comma: PENDING the same complete ordinary-variable context with NAMELIST /group_a/ a, /group_b/ b. Both slash pairs and both object lists remain present; the comma between groups is admitted rather than required.
pending.multiple-groups-without-comma: PENDING NAMELIST /group_a/ a /group_b/ b in the same context, differing only by omission of the optional intergroup comma. Do not remove an object-list comma between objects of one group.
pending.name-and-slash-repairs: PENDING separately isolated NAMELIST // a and a missing closing slash in /group_a, repaired by inserting the host-independent group name or the one missing slash. COMMON's unnamed-block alternative does not apply to NAMELIST. Keep prior object declarations and legal statement order fixed.
pending.nonempty-object-lists: PENDING an empty first or later group object list in a complete otherwise valid statement, repaired only by inserting an already declared eligible variable. A whole missing group clause, unknown variable or unsupported NAMELIST is not the selected predicate.
pending.object-comma-repairs: PENDING missing and trailing object-list comma contrasts with two distinct prior-declared variables. Distinguish an optional comma before another /group/ from a required separator between objects of the same group. Repeated object names are not inherently forbidden.
pending.shared-object-group-permission: PENDING complete compile admissions with the same eligible a in /group_a/ and /group_b/, preserving p4's nonexclusive membership permission. Declaring groups neither copies a nor transfers data; no separate no-op S effect is created for the permission.
pending.scope-order-and-name-source: PENDING finite R871/R401/R402/R603 and R504 scope relationships. NAMELIST is a specification statement and C1107 forbids it in BLOCK. Group names and object names have different productions and identity rules; actual USE/HOST/IMPORT/local routes, C8107 and19.5.1.4p2(15) must be resolved before any reuse or negative.

requirements.oracle: Complete legal declaration contexts and one-predicate group/list punctuation repairs, with shared membership admitted and exact group/object roles.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Numbered reporting is capability, not fixed English, fatal status or printed R871. Missing types/providers, invalid roles/scopes, unsupported features, source echoes and native failures do not establish a distinct grammar cause. No output or membership-value effect follows from compilation alone.

requirements.title: A namelist group object is a whole variable name
requirements.definition: A namelist-group-object is variable-name, using explicit R903/C903 rather than assumed R402. It names a variable, not a constant, expression, selected component, array element/section or new array declaration. A whole array name is possible subject to C8108, C8109 and the prior-property rules. Declaration membership and later data-transfer eligibility are separate.

pending.ordinary-variable-names: PENDING prior-declared ordinary INTEGER scalar and fixed-shape array names in a complete group. There is no I/O, undefined payload read or automatic type inference in the initial syntax control.
pending.whole-array-not-selector: PENDING prior INTEGER a(2), NAMELIST /g/ a(1), repaired by deleting only (1). This is not TARGET's array-declaration suffix. A component-selected source needs a complete accessible derived object and a whole-object repair satisfying C8109; no invalid opaque/private transfer is used as a control.
pending.constant-procedure-role-source: PENDING finite R872 -> R903/C903 relations for named constants and ordinary procedures versus variables. C903 owns the entity-role exclusion; avoid duplicate cases or forcing every named role error to be a local R872 syntax diagnostic.
pending.associated-objects-and-transfer-state-so: PENDING complete USE/HOST-associated variable admissions under p5 and14.2.2note4, and exact12.6.4.7p2 conditions for real transfer: every allocatable group object is allocated and every pointer group object is associated, not only objects named in a chosen input record. Polymorphic objects and objects with pointer/allocatable ultimate components require defined I/O. Group declaration establishes none of those states or mechanisms; no unassociated target or unallocated payload is queried.

requirements.oracle: Actual variable identities with complete declaration and whole-name controls; canonical role and transfer-state constraints stay separate.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A valid identifier does not make a parameter or procedure a variable, and grammar admission does not prove readable/definable values or I/O support. No fixture, link, profile or source-use approval is created.

requirements.title: A NAMELIST declaration does not use a USE-associated name as its group name
requirements.definition: A group name in a NAMELIST statement is not a name accessed by use association. This does not prohibit USE-associated variables as group objects, nor automatically prohibit accessing an imported group in an I/O statement. The group-name slot and object-name slots have different conditions.

pending.use-associated-group-exclusion: PENDING a complete provider module defining a public named group and a consumer that USE-associates that group, then uses its imported name as the group name in a new NAMELIST statement with a prior local INTEGER object. Repair only the new declaration's group name to a fresh local name; keep the provider and object declarations intact.
pending.renamed-group-exclusion: PENDING the same source with USE, ONLY: local_group=>provider_group and the local imported name in the NAMELIST group-name slot. Repair only that declaration name. Renaming does not make it an unrelated local group; missing module artifacts are not the cause.
pending.use-associated-object-control: PENDING a provider's public INTEGER variable imported by USE and listed as an object of a genuinely fresh local namelist group.14.2.2note4 explicitly distinguishes this legal object position from the prohibited group-name position. No forbidden attribute re-specification or runtime value read is needed.
pending.host-group-local-identity-source: PENDING exact19.5.1.4p2(15) relations: a local namelist-group-name is a local identifier and can hide a host homonym. C8107 does not say USE and HOST are identical. P3 continuation applies in one scoping unit, not automatically across those distinct groups; IMPORT/C8106 may add independent restrictions.

requirements.oracle: Complete provider/consumer name-role contrasts with one-name repairs and exact use/host/local association paths.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not turn this into a ban on using an imported group for transfer or importing group members. Keyword matching, missing providers and unqualified host-shadow assumptions do not establish the predicate.

requirements.title: Assumed-size arrays are not namelist group objects
requirements.definition: A namelist group object is not an assumed-size array. Its actual declared role and array category matter, not the appearance of a star anywhere in the file. This is not a general ban on arrays, assumed shape or every dummy object, and a selected array element is not an allowed R872 repair.

pending.assumed-size-dummy-exclusion: PENDING a complete module subroutine s(a) with prior INTEGER a(*) and NAMELIST /g/ a, repaired only by replacing * with : in its declaration. The module supplies an explicit interface; no invocation or data transfer is needed and a is a real data dummy.
pending.assumed-shape-dummy-control: PENDING the resulting nonpointer nonallocatable assumed-shape dummy, plus an ordinary constant-bound array control. Prior rank/type conditions hold. These are admissions, not runtime size/bounds or allocation observations.
pending.star-role-and-other-rank-source: PENDING original8.5.8.5/.6/.7 and R872 identity relationships. A named implied-shape constant is not a variable control, and replacing a by a(1) violates the name-only group-object grammar. Assumed-rank, pointer and allocatable alternatives need their genuine declaration and transfer premises; no automatic support or empty-array proxy is assumed.

requirements.oracle: Actual assumed-size dummy versus a minimally repaired explicit-interface assumed-shape dummy, with rank/type and group syntax unchanged.
requirements.oracle_limitation: An error in the dummy declaration or unsupported assumed-shape/NAMELIST feature does not qualify this cause. No call, missing main, undefined value or source-only star classifier is an effect.

requirements.title: Enumeration-type variables and enumeration-typed direct components are excluded
requirements.definition: A namelist group object is neither of enumeration type nor an object having a direct component of enumeration type. Direct component is the recursive3.30.1/7.5.1p4 concept: it includes immediate components and continues through nonpointer nonallocatable derived components. This is not just one level, arbitrary pointer reachability or the distinct interoperable enum type of7.6.1. C8109 has no defined-I/O exception.

pending.enumeration-variable-exclusion: PENDING a complete F2023 module defining an ENUMERATION TYPE with two valid enumerators, a TYPE(choice) variable and an ordinary INTEGER item. NAMELIST /g/ choice_value is repaired only to list item instead. Keep the enumeration definition and variable in the control so unsupported enumeration syntax cannot masquerade as the NAMELIST cause; no object value is read.
pending.immediate-enumeration-component: PENDING a complete derived type with a plain component of that previously defined enumeration type, a variable of the derived type and a separate ordinary scalar. Repair only the group object name to the scalar, retaining all type definitions in both sources. The component is a direct component and no I/O or inaccessible representation is used.
pending.recursive-nonpointer-nonallocatable-path: PENDING a plain outer derived component whose type has an enumeration component. Recursing through that nonpointer nonallocatable component makes the enumeration component direct under7.5.1p4. Parent-component/inheritance variants need their complete extension/type identities; a shallow component-only scan is not the oracle.
pending.component-attribute-boundary: PENDING the distinction between an immediate component of enumeration type, which is itself direct even if it has POINTER or ALLOCATABLE, and an enumeration object behind a component of a different derived type. Establish legal component declarations first. No pointer association/allocation query or payload transfer is needed for the membership restriction.
pending.pointer-allocatable-hop-boundary: PENDING finite source trees where a derived-type POINTER or ALLOCATABLE component cuts recursion to deeper enumeration components for the direct-component definition.12.6.4.7p2 independently requires defined I/O for an object with a pointer/allocatable ultimate component, and group-object allocation/association must hold. Conversely, supplying defined I/O does not exempt an actual enumeration-typed direct component from C8109. No blanket deep-reachability exclusion or automatic positive runtime is inferred.
pending.enum-versus-enumeration-source: PENDING original7.6.1 versus7.6.2 type/category controls. An interoperable enum type and its integer enumerators are not enumeration type; an enumerator named constant is not a variable group object. No INTEGER substitute, unsupported-feature success or unqualified companion/representation claim closes an enumeration facet.

requirements.oracle: Complete actual F2023 type graphs and source-minimal object-name repairs retaining the same type support in both programs. Apply the recursive direct-component definition independently.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source support is not compiler support. Rejection at ENUMERATION TYPE before a valid control compiles cannot prove C8109. Direct, ultimate and potential-subobject components differ; no object traversal or transfer is implemented.

requirements.title: Namelist output values follow group object-list order
requirements.definition: Values on namelist output appear in the order of the objects in the group's object list. This is an output-order requirement, not an input-order restriction: namelist input may use another order or omit objects. Record breaks, value editing and defined I/O retain their own rules.

pending.distinct-scalar-output-order: PENDING a complete real program with defined default INTEGER first=11 and second=23, a group declared in the order second,first and a synchronous actual namelist WRITE to a successfully opened scratch file. Independently observe the ordered name/value sequence SECOND=23 then FIRST=11, with exact write/read/check/completion events. An alphabetic sort, aggregate sum or READ-back alone cannot establish this order.
pending.array-then-scalar-order: PENDING a complete fixed two-element INTEGER array with independent11/13 values followed by a scalar17. Observe the expanded array values before the scalar's values using an independently justified coordinate/sequence oracle. Array element order remains9.5.3.3/12.6.3; zero-size or character exceptions do not replace nonempty evidence.
pending.portable-output-observer: PENDING a finite intrinsic-INTEGER namelist record observer grounded in13.11.2/.4 and13.10.4. Preserve uppercase names, &group and slash syntax, legal spaces/separators and processor-chosen record boundaries/widths; do not compare one compiler's pretty-printed bytes. Bound reads, check all IOSTAT/EOF/close results, reject truncation and incomplete records, and avoid arbitrary record-count or fixed-width assumptions. Character, REAL, complex, DELIM/DECIMAL, repeated-array constants and defined-I/O forms remain additional explicit gates.
pending.whole-parent-sensitivity: PENDING actual complete-parent wrong-order, wrong-value, missing-object/record/check and no-op observer countermodels, after a current passing parent. The checker must distinguish a reversed sequence that a namelist READ would still accept. No external generated fixture or compiler consensus is the semantic oracle.

requirements.oracle: Observed complete namelist output with independently established finite values and list positions, using a source-qualified record observer and complete lifecycle guards.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No executable or record parser is supplied. Successful WRITE or read-back proves neither order nor the whole formatting standard; processor-dependent record lengths/widths and defined I/O must not be narrowed silently.

requirements.title: Every repeated group-object occurrence contributes its value on output
requirements.definition: When a variable occurs multiple times in one group's object list, its value appears on output once for each occurrence. The list is not a set of unique variables. Repetition in declaration lists is distinct from repeated assignments in namelist input and from permitted compression of successive identical values within one group object's output.

pending.separated-repeated-scalar: PENDING a real output parent for group order a,b,a with defined INTEGER a=11,b=23. Observe three name/value occurrences in that order, including two separate appearances of a's value; a read-back-only oracle could miss the omitted duplicate and is insufficient.
pending.adjacent-repeated-scalar: PENDING group order a,a with one defined scalar and a complete intrinsic-INTEGER output observer. Verify both required value occurrences and suitable-input/group-object structure under13.11.3.2/.4.3, not a generic deduplicating map or a repeat notation that would supply excess values to a scalar.
pending.repeated-array-occurrence-source: PENDING a nonempty fixed array appearing twice, with independent distinct element values and the full repeated sequence. Array-element and name/value-subsequence rules, not only total counts, determine the observer. Zero-sized and character cases need separate qualification.
pending.compression-and-input-boundary: PENDING exact13.11.4.3p1 repetition-compression scope and13.11.3.1/.2 input semantics. Permitted r*c for identical values is not blanket permission to discard declaration occurrences or to demand declaration-order input. Full-program missing-duplicate sensitivity must demonstrate the distinction.

requirements.oracle: Actual output occurrence/value sequences and counters against literal expectations, with deliberate dropped/reordered duplicate countermodels.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No cases or parser are implemented. A same final value after READ, successful serialization or unique-name dictionary does not prove multiplicity. Keep canonical formatting and input rules separate.

requirements.title: Repeated local group declarations append their object lists
requirements.definition: Each successive appearance of a group name in NAMELIST statements of one scoping unit continues that group's object list. Repeating the group is permitted, and neither the last declaration alone nor a set-union of unique members replaces the concatenated list. Different scoping units can identify different groups despite a shared spelling.

pending.same-statement-continuation: PENDING a complete local NAMELIST /g/ a /g/ b with prior variables and a real output observation of the joined a,b order. Preserve optional intergroup comma alternatives as grammar controls, not duplicate execution credit.
pending.successive-statement-continuation: PENDING separate NAMELIST /g/ a and NAMELIST /g/ b,a statements, followed by a real output requiring the full a,b,a sequence. Independent values and reached occurrence counts must reject last-list replacement and deduplication.
pending.interleaved-group-lists: PENDING declarations extending g, then a different h, then g again in the same scope. Each group's list is accumulated independently in its own order. One object can belong to both under p4 without a copied-object or alias-relaxation claim.
pending.scope-and-occurrence-source: PENDING source graphs distinguishing same-scope continuation, prohibited USE-associated group re-declaration under C8107 and a local group that hides a host homonym under19.5.1.4p2(15). Complete output observers and canonical relationships remain pending; name-token equality across files is insufficient.

requirements.oracle: Exact declaration-order list concatenation with actual nonempty output/value observations and separately checked group identity.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No fixture or graph is supplied. C815's attribute-uniqueness rule is not used to ban this expressly permitted repeated group. Compile-only acceptance does not establish appended runtime output.

requirements.title: Group objects have their type, kind parameters and rank established through a permitted route
requirements.definition: A group object is accessed by use or host association, or its declared type, kind type parameters and rank are established by prior statements in the same scoping unit or by the applicable implicit typing rules. These are alternative routes, not a universal requirement for a new explicit local declaration. The first sentence specifically names kind parameters and rank; later implicit-type confirmation has its own condition.

pending.prior-explicit-properties: PENDING complete prior INTEGER declarations for a scalar and fixed array before NAMELIST, with any kind expression using an actually supported previously established kind. No initializer or I/O is required for this source/admission control.
pending.use-associated-properties: PENDING a complete provider module exporting an ordinary scalar/array object, used by a consumer's fresh local group. The provider establishes its properties; C8107 restricts the group-name slot, not this object route.
pending.host-associated-properties: PENDING a contained procedure naming an actual host variable in a fresh local group without redeclaring it. Resolve IMPORT/default host access and avoid local shadowing; a local type statement would create a different object.
pending.late-rank-source-contrast: PENDING an implicitly scalar name in NAMELIST followed by a later DIMENSION array declaration, repaired by moving the dimension specification before the NAMELIST. Adjudicate actual prior type/rank and canonical declaration constraints before a negative reporting policy; no unrelated IMPLICIT NONE or assumed-size defect is introduced.
pending.implicit-scalar-control: PENDING a deliberate nonnull implicit INTEGER mapping and a scalar n first appearing as a namelist group object. Its implicit type/default kind/rank are real properties, not unspecified until an explicit declaration. No value is read before definition.
pending.kind-length-and-state-boundaries: PENDING exact prior type/kind/rank versus CHARACTER length and derived type-parameter conditions under8.2/8.7/10.1.11. Optional kinds, deferred/assumed parameters, pointer/allocation and I/O state need their own premises. Do not expand the text into a blanket prior-known-storage-size or initialized-value requirement.

requirements.oracle: Complete finite declaration/association/implicit-mapping graphs and precisely qualified ordering controls.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The prose does not itself require fatal rejection or prescribe a message. Unknown types, invalid implicit contexts or unsupported kind probes are not a different ordering predicate; metadata/source evidence remains pending.

requirements.title: Later declarations of implicitly typed group objects confirm the implied type and parameters
requirements.definition: If a group object was typed by implicit typing rules, a subsequent type declaration confirms that implied type and its parameters. The condition is not applied indiscriminately to a prior explicitly typed or associated object, and changing a letter's assumed default without reading the actual implicit mapping is not a valid oracle.

pending.later-matching-type-control: PENDING a complete ordinary unit with the real default INTEGER mapping for n, NAMELIST /g/ n followed by INTEGER n. There is no earlier explicit declaration, NULL mapping or DATA/PARAMETER role; no runtime value is read.
pending.later-different-type-source: PENDING the same context followed by REAL n, repaired only to INTEGER n. Confirm the actual mapping and other declaration rules; any negative contract needs an independently established numbered/name-scope or explicit policy basis rather than treating this prose as required fatal diagnosis.
pending.length-kind-mapping-source: PENDING a complete custom IMPLICIT CHARACTER(LEN=2) mapping for c, NAMELIST /g/ c, and a later length-changing CHARACTER declaration, repaired to length2. Additional kind contrasts require actual supported distinct kinds, not guessed numeric IDs; p5's confirmation includes implied parameters.
pending.prior-explicit-and-associated-boundary: PENDING a prior explicitly declared LOGICAL n or a genuine use/host-associated entity in the group. The default first-letter INTEGER mapping does not override those routes. Duplicate explicit declarations, association restrictions and C815 retain their own ownership; no blanket retyping rule is invented.

requirements.oracle: Actual implicit-map and statement-order source contrasts with conforming one-change repairs and explicit scope/type-parameter prerequisites.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No compiler observation or policy is supplied. A NULL implicit mapping, unsupported kind or already-explicit duplicate declaration cannot stand in for the conditional later-confirmation requirement.

accounting.rationale: Defines the named-data group and its data-transfer reference purpose. Actual transfer semantics retain12.6/13.11; membership declaration is not a new no-op S effect.
Group objects are named data objects with R872/C903 variable identity and the local restrictions, not arbitrary output expressions.
The group name identifies the collection for transfer; it neither copies nor initializes the member variables.
12.6.2.1C1216/C1217 and13.11 retain the actual NML transfer and formatting conditions. A declaration alone creates no I/O observation or source-use link.
A member can belong to multiple groups. R871's finite admission plan preserves this permission without a duplicate S/no-op effect, copied object or inferred runtime transfer.
Membership is not exclusive to one group; each group's own output list/order semantics remain operative.
The same underlying object can be selected by different group names. No declaration copies its value or changes alias, definition or lifetime rules.
The NLIST/A,B,C example illustrates syntax only; declarations, scope and any data transfer are omitted.
The paired slashes surround one group name, not blank common or a value delimiter.
The three names must resolve to eligible variables with established properties in any completed fixture.
No initial values, actual I/O, physical record format, processor result or new normative clause is supplied.

review_rationale: Independent complete original NAMELIST source/condition/fine-atom/all47pending-plan review299b551230624de23003dffbb6af952f7a7e76df3832e15947d14541cdff9c98, registered in doc/source_audits/batch_083.json. R871 preserves named slash-delimited groups, nonempty object lists and optional intergroup comma. R872 uses explicit R903/C903 whole variable-name, not arbitrary designators; group-name uses assumed R402. C8107 excludes a USE-associated group declaration name, not associated member variables or imported-group I/O use; local host homonyms are distinct entities. C8108 needs an actual assumed-size dummy and complete assumed-shape repair. C8109 is specific to enumeration types; direct-component recursion traverses plain nonpointer nonallocatable derived/parent components, and an immediate enumeration-typed pointer/allocatable component remains direct. A deeper pointer/allocatable-derived hop cuts recursion without waiving12.6.4.7p2 allocation/association/defined-I/O prerequisites, which concern the whole group. Defined I/O never waives C8109. Five S meanings retain output order, repeated occurrences, same-scope concatenation, prior type/kind/rank and conditional later implicit confirmation. Independent literal/name/sequence observers are required: NAMELIST READ-back cannot prove output order or multiplicity. Legal format variation/compression, source/state and complete-parent sensitivity gates remain. The review verifies53original sections/470units and complete grammar heads. All47facets remain pending with no parser, native execution, fixture, canonical-link or SourceUse approval.
